session: Session 2 · Yellow Pages (30 Oct) · Nick Goh
topic: Building an AI marketing team: a lite agentic workflow with Claude

games.title: La Brigata

pairs.output: Draft brief from the project context: goal, audience, budget, timing
A verdict and the top fixes, after critiquing the brief in a fresh chat
The Big Idea one-pager, built from the validated brief
Key visual concepts and assets, using connectors such as Higgsfield
A messaging hierarchy adapted into channel-by-channel copy
Edits and sign-off, after checking work against brand voice and the Big Idea

games.intro: Nick's AI marketing team works like a kitchen brigade: a planning team and a production team. Tap a chef, then tap the dish that chef sends out. +20 for a match, −5 for a wrong plate.
games.outputsTitle: What comes out of the kitchen
games.winText: The brigade is staffed: {score} Parmigiano points

games.title: Passa il Piatto
games.scoring: 100 if first check is correct, -20 per failed check, minimum 20

strategist.hint: Digests the brief, shapes the Big Idea

you.label: You

games.recap: Brief Writer drafts → Brief Validator checks it in a new chat with fresh eyes → Strategist shapes the Big Idea → **you** approve and save it to the knowledge base → Designer + Copywriter make KVs via Higgsfield plus channel messaging → Reviewer checks brand voice. The human sign-off sits in the middle, before anything is produced.

games.poolEmptyMsg: Everyone is on the pass. Tap a step to send it back.
games.winText: The plate made it down the chain: {score} Parmigiano points

games.title: Il Quiz di Nick

questions.question: What kicks off the Marketing Brief Builder in Nick’s setup?
options: A student types the whole brief by hand
A scheduled task: Claude checks the inbox daily for the latest "Marketing Brief" email
questions.explanation: The Email Trigger: the Marketing Brief Builder runs as a scheduled task, finds the latest email labelled "Marketing Brief" and drafts from it.

questions.question: Why does the Brief Validator critique the brief in a new chat?
options: Fresh eyes: it is not anchored on the conversation that wrote the draft
Because skills only work in new chats
questions.explanation: The handoff chain says it plainly: "New chat, fresh eyes." It checks objective, audience, message and metric, then returns a verdict and top fixes.

questions.question: Step 4 of the handoff chain belongs to…
options: You, the human: approve and save to the knowledge base
questions.explanation: A person signs off on the strategy before any production starts, and the approved work becomes shared context for the rest of the team.

questions.question: What is the Strategist’s output?
questions.explanation: The Strategist digests the validated brief, develops the Big Idea and outputs a one-pager.

questions.question: Put the Terra messaging layers in campaign order (weeks 1–3, 4–6, 7–12).
options: Made to Be Kept → Nothing to Explain → The Art of Renewal
Nothing to Explain → The Art of Renewal → Made to Be Kept
The Art of Renewal → Made to Be Kept → Nothing to Explain
questions.explanation: Object first ("Nothing to Explain"), then the material story ("The Art of Renewal"), then longevity ("Made to Be Kept").

questions.question: Asked to swap a real brand ambassador’s face into the generated image, Claude…
options: Declined: a realistic likeness of a real person could read as a real endorsement or an official ad
questions.explanation: It offered to keep a clearly fictional model instead, and noted the real ambassador should not be generated or composited for anything that leaves the team.

questions.question: How were unverified material claims (like recycled-material percentages) handled?
options: Flagged "[to verify]" and kept out of the copy until confirmed
questions.explanation: Throughout the workflow, anything not yet verified was marked "[to verify]" or "[confirm]" instead of being stated as fact.

questions.question: The Creative Review Scorer judged work through which agency lenses?
questions.explanation: Each execution got a BBH, Ogilvy and McCann score, plus strengths, weaknesses and a suggestion.

questions.question: Which execution scored highest?
questions.explanation: The close-up of a hand just about to open the bag carried desire and anticipation with no claim needed, so it beat the desert story and post.

questions.question: Which pair of tools generated the key visuals and motion?
questions.explanation: The Designer / Art Director used connectors like Higgsfield, with ChatGPT images and Cinema Studio for the motion pieces.

games.intro: Ten questions on the workflow and the fictional Terra campaign. 10 points each.
games.perfectText: Ten for ten. Nick would give this a 10/10 creative score

page.blurb: Building an AI marketing team: a lite agentic workflow with Claude, with Nick Goh. Staff the kitchen brigade, pass the plate down the handoff chain and survive Nick's quiz on the Terra campaign.
